pr.title: Warn on every command when a newer release is out
pr.head: 76527ef5d7f6ea7b0777e7d94f708a8f62052255

summary: An old project beside newer skills fails with argparse's invalid choice, which reads as a broken CLI rather than an old one, and nothing between upgrades says a release is out. Every Projector skill runs project, so this pull request has the CLI itself say so: every command installed from a release prints one stderr line when the release project upgrade would install is newer.

The check reads that release's version from its plugin manifest, which carries the CLI's version too. It runs at most once a day, waits at most two seconds, and caches the answer in $XDG_CACHE_HOME/projector/release.json. It never touches stdout or the exit status, stays quiet for --help, --version, upgrade, and checkout installs, and also follows a usage error, because a usage error is what a newer skill meets on an old command.

Auto-upgrade was considered and set aside: it would run a downloaded installer with nobody present, replace the CLI under a review loop's parallel commands, and still leave the running session on the old skills until a restart.

cards.title: When the warning prints
cards.html:
InvocationWarns
Any subcommand, release install, behind the releaseYes, before the command runs
Usage error (exit 2)Yes, after argparse's error
--help, --version, --package-dirNo
upgradeNo
Checkout or editable installNo; never checks
Not installed, as the site action runs it from PYTHONPATHNo; never checks

cards.title: Configuration surface
cards.html:
• PROJECTOR_REF picks the release compared against, default v0, the same one upgrade installs. Setting it to a tag such as v0.6.2 pins and silences the warning.
  • PROJECTOR_OFFLINE skips the fetch and warns only from the cache.
  • XDG_CACHE_HOME moves the cache, default ~/.cache. A cache that cannot be written skips the fetch.
  • RELEASE_CHECK_SECONDS is one day and RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT two seconds; neither is configurable.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• The first head, 8927044, drew two findings. The two-second urlopen timeout bounded each socket step, not the fetch, so four packet-dropping addresses held a command for 8 seconds. And a cache that could not be written made every command fetch.
  • 18ba1c7 runs the fetch in a daemon thread joined for the timeout, and 76527ef records each check before fetching and skips the fetch when that write fails.
  • The review of 76527ef verified both fixes against a local server and TEST-NET addresses and found the head clean, with suggestions only.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• Auto-upgrade, for the reasons in the summary above.
  • Refreshing the release on a usage error, and keeping a fetch that lands after the wait, both flagged in the first group.
  • A module-wide stub of the check in the tests, flagged in the second group.

groups.title: The release check
groups.kicker: How a command finds the release, caches it, bounds the wait, and warns
intro: The check sits in cli.py beside run_upgrade, because it compares against the release upgrade installs: release_manifest_url derives the repository from pip's install record and the ref from PROJECTOR_REF, the same way release_installer does.

latest_release answers from the cache for a day. When the cache is older, it first records the check with the version it already knew, then fetches. Recording first means a failed fetch waits a day like a successful one, parallel commands started meanwhile read the fresh record instead of fetching too, and a cache that cannot be written skips the fetch altogether.

fetch_release_version runs urlopen in a daemon thread and joins it for two seconds, because urlopen's timeout applies to each socket operation and name resolution has none. main calls warn_of_stale_release before running any command but upgrade, and parse calls it after a usage error.
concepts: A release install is one whose pip direct_url.json has no dir_info: an archive or a Git URL. Checkout and editable installs never check.
The cache records when a check ran, not only what it found, so its timestamp is what rate-limits the network.
The CLI's version and the plugin manifest's version are one number, which the packaging tests pin.

checks.text: The warning prints only from the main thread, to stderr, and before run() or after argparse's error, so stdout, --json output, and the exit status are the command's own.
latest_release calls record_release before fetch_release_version and returns without fetching when that write fails.
The worker thread is a daemon and is joined only for RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT; a fetch that finishes later appends to a list nobody reads, and prints nothing.
newer_release compares versions as tuples of integers and returns false unless both are plain dotted numbers, so a manifest's text reaches the terminal only when it is a version.

A usage error answers from the day-old cache like any other command. That error most often comes from skills a new release just updated, which is when the cache most likely predates the release, so the warning can stay silent for up to a day exactly when it would explain the failure. Refreshing on a usage error, still under the timeout, would close that gap.

A fetch that lands after the two-second wait is dropped, and the record written before it holds off the next try for a day. On a link where the fetch always takes longer, the warning never appears; having the worker call record_release on success would keep a late answer whenever the command outlives it.

files.note: The new functions after run_upgrade, and parse and main at the bottom, where the check runs.

groups.title: Tests for the check
groups.kicker: Thirteen tests that drive main() against a local manifest and a temporary cache
intro: StaleReleaseWarningTests serves the manifest from a file:// URL, puts the cache in a temporary XDG_CACHE_HOME, and stubs pip's install record and version, so nothing reaches the network or the real cache. Each test runs a whole command through main and reads its stderr.

Two tests came with the review fixes: one stalls urlopen and checks the command gives up after the timeout, patched to 0.2 seconds, and one puts a regular file where the cache directory belongs and checks three commands make no fetch.

checks.text: test_versions_compare_as_numbers fails if versions compare as strings, where 0.6.9 would look newer than 0.6.10.
test_a_stalled_fetch_gives_up_after_the_timeout releases its stalled thread at cleanup, and the thread's OSError is caught inside the worker.

Only this class stubs the check. Every other main() test leaves it live, so on an interpreter where projector-cli is installed from a release, the suite would fetch from GitHub and write the real ~/.cache. Setting PROJECTOR_OFFLINE and a temporary XDG_CACHE_HOME for the whole module would pin that.

files.note: The new class at the end of the file.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: Where a user learns the warning exists and how to quiet it
intro: docs/cli.md documents the warning under a new "Know when a release is out" section beside upgrade: what it prints, when it stays quiet, where the release and cache come from, and the two environment variables that quiet it. The README and docs/plugins.md each gain one sentence pointing there.

checks.text: The docs' claims match the code: at most once a day, at most two seconds, a failed check waits a day, an unwritable cache skips the check, and PROJECTOR_REF set to a release's tag silences it.

files.note: The new section is the reference; the other two files link to it.
